options.B: Dietary habits change completely during the teenage years
options.C: The lymphatic system becomes temporarily blocked by growth
options.D: Skin cells stop shedding their outer protective layers

explanation: Spot on! Surging hormones wake up our sebaceous (oil) and sweat glands, leading to extra oil and body odor. Totally normal part of growing up!

question: A patient is discouraged because their BMI hasn't budged after starting an exercise routine. What else can you suggest tracking?

options.A: Waist circumference and overall energy levels
options.B: Resting body temperature and pulse rate
options.C: Daily fluid retention and shoe size changes
options.D: Total body height measured twice a week

explanation: Spot on! When starting fitness, patients often swap fat for muscle. Checking waist size and energy levels will often show great progress before the scale moves!

question: What is the primary output of the action planning phase?

options.A: A lengthy academic textbook published for university students
options.B: An application for international political asylum
options.C: A detailed schedule of activities, responsibilities, and resources
options.D: A list of punishments for families who violate hygiene laws

explanation: An action plan clearly outlines what tasks need to be done, who is responsible, when it will occur, and what materials are needed. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h6)

question: A patient has an injury affecting the clear gel that fills the main cavity behind the lens. What is this gel called?

options.A: The vitreous humor
options.B: The corneal stroma
options.C: The pupillary fluid
options.D: The aqueous humor

explanation: The vitreous humor is the jelly-like substance that gives the eyeball its stable shape behind the lens. Keep up the good work!

question: What do we call infections that jump naturally between animals and humans?

options.A: Nosocomial infections
options.B: Autoimmune disorders
options.C: Zoonotic diseases
options.D: Chronic conditions

explanation: Zoonotic diseases are infections shared between animals and humans, like rabies or Lassa fever. Always good to keep this in mind for community health!

question: A nurse checks the BP of 20 patients, gives them a new drug, and checks their BP again a month later. Which test fits best?

options.A: Independent samples t-test
options.B: Analysis of variance (ANOVA)
options.C: Chi-square test of independence
options.D: Paired samples t-test

explanation: Because you are tracking the exact same group of patients before and after an intervention, they form a 'pair'! A paired t-test is perfect here.

question: Why do patients with severe burns or major infections need significantly more calories than usual?

options.A: Stress hormones trigger a hypermetabolic state that dramatically increases energy demand
options.B: Intravenous antibiotic medications slow down digestion and trap extra nutrients
options.C: Bed rest completely eliminates muscle mass, lowering overall energy requirements
options.D: The skin dressings trap body heat, which stops natural calorie burning

explanation: Big physical trauma puts the body into overdrive. Stress hormones flood the system, speeding up metabolism and tissue breakdown like a raging fire.

question: What federal law serves as the primary legal instrument against FGM in Nigeria?

options.A: Child Rights and Welfare Enforcement Act
options.B: Violence Against Persons Prohibition Act
options.C: National Health Insurance Scheme Act
options.D: Criminal Code and Penal Code Consolidation Act

explanation: The VAPP Act of 2015 specifically prohibits harmful traditional practices, including all types of female genital mutilation at the federal level. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why can diagnosing Pick's disease be tricky in the beginning?

options.A: Its behavioral symptoms can be mistaken for psychiatric disorders.
options.B: Standard MRI scanners cannot image the frontal lobes clearly.
options.C: Routine blood tests can easily confuse it with normal aging.
options.D: Patients usually retain perfect memory until the final days.

explanation: Because the very first signs are personality changes and apathy, doctors sometimes mistake it for depression, anxiety, or mental health issues rather than a brain disease.

question: What happens when hospital administrators treat MBO as just a bureaucratic checklist?

options.A: Patient satisfaction increases across all departments
options.B: The hospital saves money on administrative salaries
options.C: Staff quickly lose interest and trust in the process
options.D: Nurses become expert planners overnight

explanation: When MBO lacks genuine leadership commitment and becomes mere paperwork, staff view it as a burden rather than a useful tool. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why are safety changes around the house so important for Alzheimer's patients?

options.A: Impaired judgment and memory put them at high risk for accidents
options.B: Physical strength increases significantly during the middle stages
options.C: Changes in vision make it impossible for them to see furniture
options.D: They recover very slowly from minor cuts and bruises

explanation: Correct! Because memory and safety judgment fade, simple things like secured doors and hazard-free floors keep them safe from harm. Wonderful clinical judgment!

question: Why do public health educators emphasize hand hygiene and washing vegetables?

options.A: To stop bacteria from causing secondary cyst infections
options.B: To eliminate adult tapeworms living in human intestines
options.C: To remove lingering agricultural pesticides from produce
options.D: To prevent the accidental ingestion of microscopic parasite eggs

explanation: Good washing habits wash away those tiny dog-shed eggs before they can enter our mouths.

question: Why is it so urgent to use an AED immediately during a sudden cardiac arrest?

options.A: Emergency services cannot track patients without active AED pads
options.B: It replaces the need to ever perform chest compressions
options.C: It permanently cures any underlying chronic heart diseases
options.D: Survival chances drop quickly for every minute without a shock

explanation: Every single minute counts! The chance of survival goes down by about 10% for every minute a shock is delayed. Fast action saves lives.

question: What is a common emotional challenge faced by patients stuck in long-term isolation?

options.A: Complete loss of long-term memory
options.B: A sudden increase in physical stamina
options.C: Total indifference to hospital surroundings
options.D: Feelings of loneliness and anxiety

explanation: That's right. Being cut off from loved ones and normal human contact can feel really heavy, so our emotional support matters just as much as medical care!

question: Why must hospitals report certain dangerous infectious diseases to public health agencies?

options.A: To punish doctors who fail to cure their patients quickly enough
options.B: To collect cash rewards offered for rare disease discoveries
options.C: To allow government officials to audit the hospital financial accounts
options.D: To help track and control disease outbreaks in the wider community

explanation: You nailed it! Reporting helps public health authorities spot epidemics early and protect the whole community before it spreads.

question: Which white blood cells rush to the scene in large numbers during an acute infection like endometritis?

options.A: Neutrophils
options.B: Plasma cells
options.C: Eosinophils
options.D: Basophils

explanation: Neutrophils are your body's rapid-response fighters! Whenever there's a sudden, acute bacterial infection, these cells flood the area to battle the germs.

question: What is the most important piece of advice to give a patient taking a 7-day course of antibiotics for cervicitis?

options.A: Share the remaining pills with your partner to save money.
options.B: Double the next dose if you forget to take one pill.
options.C: Stop taking the pills immediately if mild stomach upset occurs.
options.D: Finish all the medication even if you start feeling better early.

explanation: Always remind patients to complete their full dose! Stopping early can cause the infection to bounce back stronger.

question: What is a common reason why vaccines accidentally freeze inside a health clinic fridge?

options.A: Setting the refrigerator temperature above plus 10 degrees Celsius
options.B: Using digital data loggers instead of paper logs
options.C: Keeping facility doors locked during weekends
options.D: Placing sensitive vaccines too close to the freezer compartment

explanation: Be careful where you place stock! The parts right next to the freezer section can easily drop below zero and ruin freeze-sensitive doses.

question: What happens when the tight seals (tight junctions) between cells in your gut get damaged?

options.A: Your body completely stops making digestive enzymes
options.B: Nutrient absorption shoots up because the spaces get wider
options.C: Peristalsis speeds up to push the damaged tissue out
options.D: Harmful substances leak into your body tissue and bloodstream

explanation: Tight junctions act like brick-and-mortar seals between your gut cells. When they break, unwanted substances slip through into the body, which can trigger inflammation.

question: Why is community-centred care considered a shift from traditional hospital nursing?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any medications or clinical equipment
options.B: It focuses only on newborn babies and ignores elderly populations
options.C: It moves the focus from treating sickness in facilities to preventing illness in neighborhoods
options.D: It relies entirely on doctors rather than nurses to provide care

explanation: Traditional nursing often waits for patients to become sick enough to enter a hospital, whereas community-centred care proactively addresses health where people live. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h1)

question: If one person in a house has scabies, why is it super important to treat everyone living in that home at the same time?

options.A: Mites spread easily through close personal contact and shared bedding
options.B: Topical creams expire quickly once opened in a shared household
options.C: Family members always develop symptoms faster than the index patient
options.D: Untreated family members will develop permanent skin scarring

explanation: Scabies mites love to hop between people through skin contact or shared blankets. Treating the whole household at once stops everyone from passing the bugs back and forth!

question: Why is accurate home care documentation especially critical compared to hospital notes?

options.A: Hospital records are destroyed as soon as the patient is discharged.
options.B: Insurance companies never read hospital charts, only home visit notes.
options.C: Home patients are legally required to keep a copy of every nurse's note.
options.D: Home nurses work independently and their notes are the main record of care.

explanation: Spot on! Since home nurses work on their own without a team standing right beside them, detailed notes are vital for tracking progress safely.

question: What exactly is an occupational health hazard?

options.A: The personal medical history of a factory worker
options.B: Only physical injuries sustained during a night shift
options.C: A financial loss experienced by a business owner
options.D: Any workplace factor that can cause injury or illness

explanation: Think of an occupational hazard as anything at work—like dust, noise, or stress—that can harm a worker's body or mind. You've got this!

question: What causes most needle-stick injuries among nursing students and staff?

options.A: Attempting to recap used needles
options.B: Administering intravenous medications too quickly
options.C: Reading patient charts near the bedside
options.D: Washing contaminated glass ampoules

explanation: Recapping used needles is a leading cause of accidental pricks because a slip of the hand means a direct puncture. Never recap if you can avoid it!

question: Which chemical compound is commonly used for disinfecting blood spills on hard surfaces due to its quick action and low cost?

options.A: Liquid paraffin oil
options.B: Normal saline solution
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide cream
options.D: Sodium hypochlorite

explanation: Sodium hypochlorite, commonly known as bleach, is an affordable and effective disinfectant for clearing up blood spills. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why are standards essential for a nurse manager within the control process?

options.A: They provide a baseline measurement to evaluate actual nursing practice
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for shift handovers
options.C: They prevent patients from ever complaining about care
options.D: They dictate the exact salary scale for each department

explanation: A standard gives managers a clear, agreed-upon target to check if the care being delivered matches what is expected. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h1)

question: Why do nurses perform a physical examination during primary health care?

options.A: To diagnose terminal illnesses exclusively
options.B: To replace the need for a patient health history
options.C: To prescribe complex surgical procedures
options.D: To detect normal and abnormal clinical findings

explanation: Spotting what's normal versus what's unusual is a core nursing skill! The physical exam helps you systematically check the body to catch any changes early. You've got this!

question: What is a confounding variable?

options.A: A measurement error made by laboratory equipment
options.B: An outside factor related to both exposure and disease
options.C: The main exposure being studied by the nurse
options.D: A deliberate intervention created by the research team

explanation: Think of a confounder as a sneaky third factor that messes with our results by hiding the true relationship between our exposure and disease.

question: Why is it helpful for nursing schools to study different learning theories?

options.A: To prevent students from ever making mistakes at the bedside
options.B: To ensure the nursing school meets strict legal building codes
options.C: To make sure students pass tests without doing clinical practice
options.D: To use evidence-based methods instead of guessing what works

explanation: Just like we use evidence-based care for patients, educators use proven learning theories so they don't have to just guess how to teach us best!

question: What sign in a patient's stool might warn a nurse about internal bleeding from an anticoagulant?

options.A: Hard and dry pebble consistency
options.B: Bright yellow discoloration
options.C: Frothy and mucus-coated texture
options.D: Dark, tarry, or bloody appearance

explanation: Keep your eyes open for 'melena' (dark, tarry stools)! It's a classic red flag that bleeding might be happening somewhere in the GI tract.

question: An 8-month-old baby comes to the clinic having missed their 14-week doses. What should you do?

options.A: Restart the entire immunization series from the very beginning
options.B: Continue the schedule from where they stopped using catch-up principles
options.C: Give only adult-strength boosters to make up for lost time
options.D: Wait until the child turns one year old before administering any new vaccines

explanation: No need to restart! Immunization schedules are cumulative. Just use catch-up principles to pick up right where they left off.

question: Which of these is NOT an ethical concern when using health wearables?

options.A: Ensuring equal access for patients regardless of income
options.B: Obtaining proper informed consent for data sharing
options.C: Protecting personal health information from data breaches
options.D: Increasing the physical battery weight of the wristband

explanation: Battery weight is just hardware design, while privacy, consent, and equal access are major ethical issues in nursing informatics.

question: A community health nurse is assigned to a quarantine camp. Which combination of tasks forms her core daily responsibility?

options.A: Enforcing court orders, arresting rulebreakers, and guarding the perimeter gate
options.B: Importing medical equipment and managing the national budget
options.C: Diagnosing new viral strains using advanced laboratory genome sequencing
options.D: Monitoring temperatures, providing health education, and offering emotional support

explanation: The nurse's core role centers on clinical monitoring, patient education, and psychosocial care within the facility. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h9)

question: Which sign around a skull pin site should ring alarm bells and be reported immediately?

options.A: A small amount of clear dried crusting
options.B: Mild redness that disappears within a day
options.C: Purulent yellow drainage and a foul odor
options.D: Normal skin color around the metal screw

explanation: Pus and bad smells always point to an infection setting in. Let the doctor know right away so it can be treated!

question: What is the main purpose of doing a baseline psychiatric assessment for a patient with a degenerative illness?

options.A: To diagnose the exact genetic mutation causing the disease
options.B: To establish a baseline for the patient's mood and cognitive status
options.C: To replace the need for a physical neurological examination
options.D: To test the patient's physical strength and balance

explanation: Taking a baseline measurement lets us see where the patient stands today, so we can track any mental or emotional changes later on.

question: What communication style should a nurse use when counseling a caregiver who defaulted on vaccines?

options.A: Total silence while the caregiver reads a pamphlet
options.B: Rapid medical terminology to prove professional status
options.C: Strict lecturing to show authority and clinical power
options.D: Respectful listening and clear, non-judgmental explanations

explanation: Caregivers respond better to patience and empathy than to strict scolding, which often makes them avoid the clinic permanently. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h5)

question: Why is low intervention fidelity a risk to a health program?

options.A: It automatically stops all funding from reaching the primary health centre
options.B: It makes community members refuse any future medical treatment
options.C: It can cause the program to fail to achieve its health goals even if completed
options.D: It forces the government to shut down the entire health district

explanation: If we skip steps or rush through procedures, the community won't get the full health benefits we promised them.

question: Why should you warn patients about mild side effects before they start a new drug?

options.A: To eliminate all possibility of severe allergic reactions developing later
options.B: To guarantee that the pharmacy receives full payment for the prescription
options.C: To prevent them from stopping the medication in panic when side effects occur
options.D: To ensure the patient stops taking the medication at the first sign of discomfort

explanation: A forewarned patient stays calm when mild side effects pop up and sticks to their treatment plan. Great patient education!

question: What key cellular sign helps a pathologist identify chronic endometritis under a microscope?

options.A: Complete absence of any immune cells
options.B: The presence of plasma cells in the endometrial stroma
options.C: Enlarged muscle fibers in the outer wall
options.D: An overwhelming number of red blood cells

explanation: While acute infections bring neutrophils, chronic (long-term) endometritis is officially diagnosed by spotting plasma cells hiding out in the tissue lining.

question: Why are progestin-only pills usually recommended for breastfeeding mothers instead of combined oral pills?

options.A: They provide permanent protection after a single dose
options.B: They do not interfere with breast milk production
options.C: They completely stop all menstrual bleeding forever
options.D: They protect the mother against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Since progestin-only pills don't have estrogen, they keep a mother's milk supply safe and flowing for her baby. Brilliant clinical reasoning!

question: Which of these is a key focus during Antenatal Care (ANC) visits in Nigerian clinics?

options.A: Treating chronic adult diabetes mellitus
options.B: Scheduling permanent surgical sterilization
options.C: Conducting forensic examinations for survivors of abuse
options.D: Screening for conditions like gestational hypertension

explanation: Great thinking! ANC visits give nurses a wonderful chance to monitor blood pressure and catch dangerous pregnancy complications early.

question: Why is rapid treatment so critical for a patient with cholera?

options.A: It prevents the spread of airborne droplets
options.B: Antibiotics stop chronic liver failure instantly
options.C: Severe fluid loss can cause death within hours
options.D: Delayed care causes permanent paralysis

explanation: The rapid loss of body water and salts can quickly lead to shock if we don't replace it right away. Quick action saves lives!

question: Why can no single health professional manage modern healthcare alone?

options.A: Because nurses now demand equal pay and authority
options.B: Because doctors refuse to work long hours without help
options.C: Because laws strictly forbid solo practice in any hospital
options.D: Because medical knowledge and patient needs are too complex

explanation: You got it! Medicine and nursing involve so many details today that no single person can know or do it all alone. Teamwork makes the dream work!

question: How does proper financial control directly help patient care?

options.A: It completely removes the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.B: It allows nurses to spend less time documenting patient symptoms
options.C: It guarantees that patients never have to wait in the emergency room
options.D: It ensures necessary equipment and medications are available when needed

explanation: When money is managed well, your ward will steadily have the tools, drugs, and supplies required to treat patients safely.

question: What is the primary clinical complication caused by the poliovirus?

options.A: Irreversible muscle paralysis in the limbs
options.B: High fever accompanied by a widespread skin rash
options.C: Uncontrollable fits of violent coughing
options.D: Severe chronic diarrhea and rapid dehydration

explanation: Poliovirus attacks the nervous system, which can lead to total, permanent paralysis, most commonly affecting the legs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h4)

question: Why is following a strict code of ethics so important for a nurse?

options.A: It ensures the nurse receives the highest possible salary tier
options.B: It eliminates the need for any formal continuing education classes
options.C: It guarantees patient confidentiality, dignity, and fairness in care
options.D: It grants the nurse legal authority to perform major surgeries

explanation: Our ethical code is our compass. It guides us to treat every patient fairly, keep their secrets safe, and always respect their human dignity. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the main job of nitric oxide when a man gets an erection?

options.A: Stimulating the sympathetic nervous system to contract the prostate
options.B: Relaxing smooth muscle to allow blood to fill the corpora cavernosa
options.C: Constricting local arteries to trap blood inside the pelvic cavity
options.D: Destroying excess fibrous tissue within the tunica albuginea

explanation: Nitric oxide acts like a smooth muscle relaxant in the blood vessels, letting blood rush in and fill the chambers (corpora cavernosa) to create firmness.

question: How should nurses view technology in home health care?

options.A: As a total replacement for in-person nursing visits
options.B: As a tool to support connection and monitoring, not replace personal touch
options.C: As an unnecessary distraction that has no clinical value
options.D: As a device that only doctors are allowed to operate

explanation: Tech is a wonderful assistant for monitoring, but it can never replace the warmth and care of a human nurse sitting by the bedside.

question: Why is pushing down on top of the mother's bump (fundal pressure) a big no-no during shoulder dystocia?

options.A: It stops the placenta from delivering after the baby
options.B: It makes the baby turn around into a breech position
options.C: It causes the mother's blood pressure to drop too low
options.D: It can cause the trapped shoulder to wedge tighter and rupture the uterus

explanation: Pushing from above only jams the shoulder harder against the bone. Avoid fundal pressure completely in shoulder dystocia!

question: What does the top number in a blood pressure reading represent?

options.A: Systolic pressure when the heart rests
options.B: Systolic pressure when the heart beats
options.C: Diastolic pressure when the heart rests
options.D: Diastolic pressure when the heart beats

explanation: The top number is the systolic pressure, which measures the force in the arteries when the heart contracts or beats. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h1)

question: What is a great way to help an elderly patient remember their daily meds?

options.A: Using a labeled weekly pill organizer and daily routine cues
options.B: Hiding the pills in food without telling the patient
options.C: Instructing them to double the dose whenever they feel worse
options.D: Telling them to stop taking all drugs if they feel normal

explanation: Pill boxes and tying meds to meal times make life so much easier for patients managing multiple prescriptions.

question: Why must anticholinergic drugs be avoided in patients with narrow-angle glaucoma?

options.A: They dilate blood vessels inside the retina
options.B: They cause permanent blindness instantly
options.C: They dissolve the cornea over time
options.D: They can dangerously increase eye pressure

explanation: Correct! Blocking acetylcholine makes the pupil widen, trapping fluid inside the eye and causing a dangerous spike in pressure.

question: Which vaccine is routinely administered to pregnant women during antenatal care visits to prevent a specific neonatal infection?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid
options.B: Measles vaccine
options.C: Oral polio vaccine
options.D: Bacille Calmette-Guérin

explanation: Pregnant women receive tetanus toxoid injections during antenatal visits to protect both mother and newborn against tetanus. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h4)

question: Which set of vital sign changes makes up the classic warning sign known as Cushing's triad?

options.A: Low temperature, slow pulse, and normal blood pressure
options.B: High fever, rapid heart rate, and low blood pressure
options.C: Widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respirations
options.D: Narrow pulse pressure, tachycardia, and deep breathing

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! Cushing's triad is a serious late warning sign that pressure inside the skull has risen to a dangerous level.

question: A mother brings her young child with sickle cell anaemia to the clinic. Which statement by the mother shows she understands home care instructions?

options.A: We stopped the daily penicillin because our child has not been sick lately
options.B: We avoid letting our child eat any green vegetables containing folic acid
options.C: I only give pain medication when the swelling in the fingers becomes unbearable
options.D: I make sure my child drinks plenty of water every day, even when feeling well

explanation: Consistent daily hydration keeps red blood cells flowing smoothly and is a cornerstone of preventing painful vaso-occlusive episodes at home. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h7)

question: What important clinical step must a nurse take before starting a returning defaulter on a new hormonal contraceptive?

options.A: Require the client to pay a fine for defaulting
options.B: Wait for laboratory tests that take three weeks
options.C: Carefully rule out existing pregnancy
options.D: Consult the national ministry of health directly

explanation: Safety first! Always rule out pregnancy before dispensing or administering new hormonal methods to protect both client and baby.

question: If you don't have a tissue handy and suddenly need to cough, what should you do?

options.A: Cough into your inner elbow
options.B: Cough directly into the open air
options.C: Turn your head toward the nearest wall
options.D: Cover your mouth with both bare hands

explanation: Brilliant! Coughing into your elbow keeps the droplets off your hands. If you cough into your hands, you'll just transfer those germs to every door handle and chart you touch!

question: What is the main danger of leaving a collected lab specimen sitting at room temperature for too long?

options.A: Bacteria can multiply and cells can break down, giving false results
options.B: The label on the container will automatically fade and fall off
options.C: The specimen container will become legally invalid for testing
options.D: Hospital management will issue a fine for delayed paperwork

explanation: Time matters! Leaving samples sitting around lets bacteria multiply or cells decay, which ruins the accuracy of the test.

question: Which of the following is an example of a posterior surface landmark?

options.A: Umbilicus
options.B: Inguinal crease
options.C: Sternal angle
options.D: Scapula

explanation: The scapula, or shoulder blade, is located on the back of the body, making it a posterior landmark. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h5)

question: In what order should you assess a patient's abdomen during a physical exam?

options.A: Inspect, then palpate, then auscultate
options.B: Inspect, then auscultate, then palpate
options.C: Auscultate, then palpate, then inspect
options.D: Palpate, then inspect, then auscultate

explanation: Always listen (auscultate) before you press (palpate)! If you press first, you might push things around and change the natural bowel sounds. Smart nursing practice!

question: What is an essential component of any upward referral from a nurse?

options.A: Cash payment for the specialist consultation at the tertiary gate
options.B: A clear clinical summary letter detailing history and current medications
options.C: A personal guarantee that the client will be admitted as an inpatient
options.D: Official approval from the local government chairman

explanation: Always send a proper handover note! A clear clinical summary helps the specialist know what you've tried and what the patient needs next.

question: Why do cities usually record higher family planning use than rural villages?

options.A: Better access to equipped health facilities and higher literacy
options.B: Rural health workers refuse to distribute any commodities
options.C: Contraceptives are strictly forbidden by law in villages
options.D: Traditional beliefs are completely absent in big cities

explanation: Being close to clinics and having better access to health education makes it much easier for city residents to get and use family planning services.

question: What happens if clinic staff ignore their daily logs and stock registers?

options.A: Patients will automatically receive better care from nursing staff
options.B: The government will instantly increase the facility's monthly budget
options.C: Infection control practices become strictly enforced by default
options.D: Stockouts of essential medicines may go unnoticed until supplies completely run out

explanation: Keeping daily records helps you spot when drugs are running low so you can reorder before empty shelves catch you by surprise.

question: What is the primary role of progesterone during the majority of a normal pregnancy?

options.A: To maintain uterine muscle relaxation and prevent early contractions
options.B: To trigger the posterior pituitary gland to release large amounts of oxytocin
options.C: To actively stimulate the frequent ripening of the uterine cervix
options.D: To raise maternal blood glucose levels for the growing fetus

explanation: Progesterone acts as a relaxant on the smooth muscle of the uterus, keeping it quiet and preventing premature labour throughout gestation. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h4)

question: A patient is in contact precautions for a resistant bug. What is the rule for gloves in this room?

options.A: Wear gloves only if the patient is bleeding
options.B: Keep the same pair on for your whole shift
options.C: Put on gloves before entering the room and remove them before leaving
options.D: Wear gloves only if doing a surgical dressing change

explanation: For contact precautions, put on your gloves right before you step into the room, and take them off before you step out to contain the germs.

question: A pregnant woman is worried about dark patches on her face and a line on her belly. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Reassure her that these are normal hormonal changes that usually fade after birth
options.B: Advise her to scrub the dark areas hard with soap every morning
options.C: Explain that these marks indicate a dangerous vitamin deficiency in her diet
options.D: Tell her to immediately see a dermatologist for emergency skin surgery

explanation: A warm, reassuring word goes a long way! Explaining that these marks are normal helps anxious mums relax.

question: Where is the pleural space actually located in the body?

options.A: Between the visceral pleura and the parietal pleura
options.B: Directly inside the chambers of the human heart
options.C: Between the skin and the outer rib cage muscles
options.D: Inside the main bronchial tubes of the lungs

explanation: Spot on! It sits neatly as a tiny space between the two membrane layers that wrap around and protect our lungs.

question: What does an electromyography (EMG) test mainly measure?

options.A: Pressure inside joint capsules
options.B: Mineral density inside long bones
options.C: Blood flow through deep leg veins
options.D: Electrical activity within skeletal muscles

explanation: An EMG uses tiny needle electrodes in the muscle to check its electrical signals. It helps doctors figure out if a problem comes from the nerve or the muscle itself.

question: A nurse wants to know if child stunting rates decreased two years after starting a food program. What action is this?

options.A: Evaluating long-term program impact
options.B: Conducting a 24-hour dietary recall
options.C: Monitoring daily vitamin distribution
options.D: Screening a child with MUAC tape

explanation: Checking rates after a long period to see if the main goal was achieved is a classic evaluation of impact. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT an advantage of using a checklist in nursing research?

options.A: Producing structured data that is easy to score
options.B: Being quick and straightforward to administer
options.C: Providing deep, emotional life stories of patients
options.D: Reducing subjective wandering during clinical observation

explanation: Checklists capture neat, measurable data—they aren't designed to tell deep, open-ended emotional stories.

question: What is the very first quick check a nurse should do during an emergency airway assessment?

options.A: Listen for tummy sounds in all four quadrants
options.B: Look, listen, and feel for air movement
options.C: Check arterial blood gas lab results
options.D: Measure the exact size of the patient's neck

explanation: Keep it simple and fast! By looking at the chest, listening near the mouth, and feeling for breath, you instantly know if air is moving in and out.

question: What is the proper thing to do with dirty bedsheets right after removing them from a patient's bed?

options.A: Fold them nicely and put them on the patient's bedside table
options.B: Place them directly into a designated laundry hamper
options.C: Drop them on the floor until you finish your shift
options.D: Spread them across a clean chair for later

explanation: Spot on! Putting dirty linens straight into the laundry basket stops germs from spreading around the ward and keeps tables clean.

question: What happens right in the center of an old TB tubercle as the infection sits there?

options.A: Caseous necrosis or cheese-like tissue death
options.B: Conversion of bacteria into normal flora
options.C: Rapid regeneration of healthy lung tissue
options.D: Calcification into solid bone-like structures

explanation: As the battle inside the tubercle continues, the center part of the tissue dies and turns into a soft, crumbly substance that looks a bit like cheese—hence 'caseous necrosis'.

question: Why is vocational training an important part of holistic fistula care?

options.A: It teaches the patient how to use specialized machinery to clean hospital linen
options.B: It helps survivors regain financial independence and rebuild their lives after social stigma
options.C: It acts as a substitute for medical treatment when surgery fails to close the hole
options.D: It trains the patient to perform minor surgical repairs on other women in the village

explanation: Great job! Learning a trade empowers these women economically, helping them bounce back from poverty and isolation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h6)

question: In community health nursing, who is considered the primary 'client'?

options.A: Only the children under five years old
options.B: The local government chairman
options.C: The medical director of the district hospital
options.D: The entire population of the community

explanation: Correct! While bedside nurses focus on one patient at a time, community health nurses look at the big picture and treat the whole population as their patient.

question: Which type of FGM involves cutting and repositioning the labia to create a covering seal over the vaginal opening?

options.A: Pricking
options.B: Scraping
options.C: Infibulation
options.D: Clitoridectomy

explanation: Great try! Infibulation (Type III FGM) narrows the vaginal opening by creating a tough seal with the labia.

question: Why do teenagers sometimes take big risks or act on impulse?

options.A: Brain development is completely finished by age ten
options.B: Parents encourage dangerous activities to build character
options.C: Teens explore identity and independence while their decision-making brain regions mature
options.D: Risky behaviors are mandatory symptoms of hormonal disease

explanation: The brain's impulse-control center is still under construction during these years, which explains why teens love quick thrills and trying new things.

question: What does active listening really mean when you are trying to negotiate for health changes?

options.A: Agreeing to all demands without questioning policies
options.B: Understanding the constraints and viewpoints of decision-makers
options.C: Taking notes only to prove the other party is wrong
options.D: Interrupting opponents to correct their facts quickly

explanation: That's right! When you listen to where decision-makers are coming from, it's much easier to find common ground and reach a good compromise.

question: What is a key nursing strategy for helping patients prevent complications from chronic skin conditions?

options.A: Teaching the patient how to recognize early flare-ups and avoid known triggers
options.B: Stopping all topical medications as soon as the skin looks slightly better
options.C: Using harsh antiseptic scrubs every day to remove the outer skin layer
options.D: Encouraging the patient to isolate themselves from family and friends

explanation: You got it! Empowering patients to spot early warning signs and steer clear of their triggers stops small issues from blowing up into major infections.

question: What is a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: An abnormal tract connecting the rectum and vagina
options.B: A complete rupture of the perineal body muscles
options.C: A prolapse of the uterine wall into the rectum
options.D: An infection of the Bartholin gland

explanation: A rectovaginal fistula creates an unwanted passage allowing bowel contents to enter the vaginal canal. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h1)

question: At what heart rate should you start chest compressions during newborn resuscitation?

options.A: Below 60 beats per minute
options.B: Below 80 beats per minute
options.C: Below 40 beats per minute
options.D: Below 100 beats per minute

explanation: If the heart rate drops below 60 despite good assisted breathing, the heart needs direct chest compressions to keep blood flowing.

question: What is the name of the most common expectorant you'll see in everyday pharmacy practice?

options.A: Diphenhydramine
options.B: Salbutamol
options.C: Guaifenesin
options.D: Dextromethorphan

explanation: That's it! Guaifenesin is the go-to active ingredient in almost all chest congestion syrups you see on the shelves.

question: What happens when a country experiences rapid population growth without adequate family planning?

options.A: Hospitals experience a permanent surplus of medical supplies
options.B: Public infrastructure like schools and hospitals becomes overwhelmed
options.C: Educational standards automatically rise across all regions
options.D: The national economy instantly becomes the richest in the world

explanation: Uncontrolled population growth outpaces the government's ability to build and maintain essential public services and facilities. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h5)

question: What type of leadership style involves inviting input from team members before making decisions?

options.A: Democratic leadership
options.B: Bureaucratic leadership
options.C: Laissez-faire leadership
options.D: Autocratic leadership

explanation: Democratic leaders encourage participation and value input from the entire team when planning or solving problems. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h3)

question: A nurse notices feelings of personal discomfort when caring for a transgender patient. What is the most professional initial step to take?

options.A: Gently advise the patient to alter their outward gender expression
options.B: Ask another nurse to take over the assignment without explanation
options.C: Reflect on personal biases to ensure they do not affect the quality of care
options.D: Ignore the discomfort and assume it will go away on its own

explanation: Self-reflection is vital for nurses to manage personal attitudes so they can deliver objective, compassionate care to every patient regardless of background. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h8)

question: Why should you be extra careful using thermal compresses on patients with diabetic neuropathy?

options.A: It automatically causes severe allergic reactions to moisture
options.B: It prevents the compress material from sticking to the skin surface
options.C: It speeds up blood sugar absorption into local muscles dangerously
options.D: Patients cannot accurately feel temperature extremes to warn of tissue damage

explanation: When nerve sensation is damaged, patients might not feel if the compress is burning them until real injury has already happened. Safety first!

question: A nurse wants to understand the daily emotional experiences of mothers caring for children with chronic kidney disease. Which approach is best?

options.A: Qualitative phenomenology
options.B: Epidemiological survey
options.C: Quantitative correlational
options.D: Experimental clinical trial

explanation: Phenomenology sounds like a big word, but it just means studying the 'lived experience' of people going through a specific life event. Perfect for capturing their real stories!

question: Why do we investigate an incident after a workplace injury happens?

options.A: To prove to external inspectors that the company has no safety rules
options.B: To find a way to punish the injured worker for being clumsy
options.C: To discover the root causes and prevent similar accidents from happening again
options.D: To increase the speed of production machinery in the factory

explanation: An incident investigation is never about blaming someone. It's about playing detective to fix the system so the exact same accident never happens to anyone else.

question: Why must a nurse know the specific type of FGM a patient has experienced?

options.A: It determines the appropriate legal fine for the family
options.B: It dictates the patient's future career choices
options.C: It guides the exact surgical and obstetric management needed
options.D: It predicts the exact age when the procedure was done

explanation: Spot on! Different types involve different levels of tissue removal, which tells you what kind of clinical care or surgery she might need. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why must school management set aside specific funds in their yearly budget for health?

options.A: To purchase luxury furniture for administrative offices
options.B: To pay for students' personal family medical bills
options.C: To purchase medical supplies and maintain health facilities
options.D: To fund international educational excursions

explanation: You nailed it! Having dedicated funds means first-aid items, cleaning products, and clinic tools are always ready when emergencies happen.

question: A teenager comes in with severe monthly belly pain but no menstrual bleeding. Which condition is the most likely cause?

options.A: Bacterial vaginosis
options.B: Vaginal agenesis
options.C: Atrophic vaginitis
options.D: Transverse vaginal septum

explanation: Well done! A transverse septum acts like a wall blocking menstrual blood from getting out, leading to trapped blood, swollen tissues, and intense monthly pain even though her uterus is working fine.

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of a localized infection following suture removal?

options.A: Mild itching around the adhesive strips
options.B: Temporary skin numbness near the cut
options.C: Pus drainage and spreading skin warmth
options.D: Fading pink color of the scar line

explanation: Pus and warmth indicate bacterial multiplication and active inflammation, which signal that the wound is becoming infected. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)
